name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
description: Enhances immunity, relieves respiratory ailments, and acts as a powerful adaptogen to reduce stress and anxiety.
uses: Relieves cough, cold, fever, and respiratory congestion; reduces stress and promotes mental clarity.
preparation: Boil 5-7 fresh leaves in water for 5 minutes to make a warm herbal tea (Kashaya).
safety_notes: May lower blood sugar; exercise caution if taking anti-diabetic medications.

name: Ashwagandha (Indian Ginseng)
description: Promotes physical stamina, reduces cortisol levels, improves sleep quality, and strengthens muscle recovery.
uses: Alleviates anxiety, chronic fatigue, muscle weakness, and supports male reproductive health.
preparation: Mix 1/2 teaspoon of root powder (Churna) with warm milk and honey before sleep.
safety_notes: Avoid during acute hyperthyroidism and pregnancy unless prescribed by a Vaidya.

name: Neem
description: Potent blood purifier, anti-bacterial agent, and excellent remedy for skin conditions, acne, and oral health.
uses: Clears acne, skin rashes, purifies blood, and maintains healthy gums.
preparation: Crush fresh leaves into a paste for external skin application or consume diluted leaf juice sparingly.
safety_notes: Extremely bitter and cold; long-term internal use is not recommended for Vata-dominant individuals.

name: Amla (Indian Gooseberry)
description: Exceptionally rich in natural Vitamin C, promotes longevity, aids digestion, and strengthens hair and immunity.
uses: Promotes eye health, enhances digestion, prevents premature hair graying, and boosts immunity.
preparation: Consume 10-15 ml fresh juice daily on an empty stomach or eat fresh raw fruit.
safety_notes: May cause dryness in excessive amounts due to its astringent nature.

name: Turmeric (Haldi)
description: Natural anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, wound healer, and digestive fire (Agni) enhancer.
uses: Heals wounds, reduces joint pain, cleanses skin complexion, and boosts immunity.
preparation: Mix 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder in warm milk (Golden Milk) with a pinch of black pepper.
safety_notes: High doses may irritate stomach lining or aggravate Pitta heat.

name: Aloe Vera (Ghritakumari)
description: Soothes internal heat and skin inflammation, aids smooth digestion, and detoxifies the liver.
uses: Treats skin burns, relieves constipation, improves liver health, and cools acid reflux.
preparation: Extract fresh clear gel from the inner leaf and blend with equal parts water.
safety_notes: Do not consume the yellow outer latex layer as it acts as a harsh laxative.

name: Brahmi (Gotu Kola)
description: Promotes mental clarity, enhances memory retention, calms nervous tension, and reduces mental fatigue.
uses: Enhances memory, aids concentration, calms anxiety, and improves sleep.
preparation: Infuse 1 teaspoon dried herb in hot water for tea or consume as a ghee formulation (Brahmi Ghrita).
safety_notes: May cause mild headache or stomach distress in high doses.

name: Ginger (Shunti)
description: Ignites Agni (digestive fire), reduces motion sickness and nausea, and relieves joint stiffness.
uses: Stimulates appetite, eases nausea, aids bloating, and reduces cold symptoms.
preparation: Boil sliced fresh ginger root in water with lemon and honey to make tea.
safety_notes: Avoid excessive consumption in bleeding disorders or severe hyperacidity.

name: Cardamom (Elaichi)
description: Relieves indigestion, reduces intestinal gas, freshens breath, and calms acid reflux.
uses: Freshens breath, relieves flatulence, calms nausea, and enhances spice digestion.
preparation: Crush 2-3 pods into herbal tea, warm milk, or culinary dishes.
safety_notes: Generally very safe; large doses should be avoided by gallstone sufferers.

name: Giloy (Guduchi)
description: Improves white blood cell counts, reduces chronic fevers, and detoxifies deep tissues.
uses: Reduces recurrent fevers, boosts platelet counts, detoxifies blood, and aids arthritis.
preparation: Boil dried stem pieces in water until liquid reduces to one-fourth (Kwatha).
safety_notes: May stimulate the immune system; monitor carefully in autoimmune conditions.

name: Shatavari
description: Primary rejuvenative tonic for female reproductive health, hormonal balance, and vitality.
uses: Supports lactation, balances female hormones, eases menopausal symptoms, and soothes ulcers.
preparation: Mix 1 teaspoon powdered root with warm milk and a sweetener once daily.
safety_notes: Avoid in cases of high Kapha congestion or estrogen-sensitive conditions without advice.

name: Moringa (Drumstick Tree / Shigru)
description: Nutrient-dense superfood supporting bone density, joint flexibility, and metabolic health.
uses: Relieves joint inflammation, fights malnutrition, supports bone health, and regulates blood sugar.
preparation: Mix 1/2 teaspoon dried leaf powder into warm water, soups, or smoothies.
safety_notes: Roots and bark extracts should be avoided during pregnancy.

name: Haritaki
description: Cleanses the digestive tract, promotes bowel regularity, and supports healthy tissue regeneration.
uses: Relieves chronic constipation, purifies colon, improves vision, and strengthens teeth.
preparation: Take 1/2 teaspoon powder with warm water at bedtime.
safety_notes: Avoid during pregnancy, dehydration, or acute exhaustion.

name: Bibhitaki
description: Supports respiratory health, clears excess bronchial mucus, and forms part of the Triphala formulation.
uses: Clears bronchial phlegm, relieves sore throat, supports hair health, and reduces Kapha stagnation.
preparation: Gargle warm decoction of fruit powder for sore throat or consume with honey.
safety_notes: Excessive consumption can cause dryness or mild constipation.

name: Arjuna
description: Renowned cardio-protective tonic that strengthens cardiac muscles and supports healthy blood pressure.
uses: Strengthens heart muscles, supports vascular health, and helps maintain healthy lipid levels.
preparation: Boil bark powder in milk and water mixture to make Arjuna Ksheerapaka.
safety_notes: Consult a cardiologist if currently taking cardiac medication.

name: Bhringraj
description: Promotes dense hair growth, prevents premature hair graying, and supports liver rejuvenation.
uses: Prevents hair loss, cools head heat, improves liver function, and supports skin health.
preparation: Apply infused sesame/coconut hair oil (Bhringraj Taila) directly to scalp.
safety_notes: Internal leaf juice is cold; avoid applying oil overnight if prone to sinusitis.

name: Fenugreek (Methi)
description: Regulates blood sugar metabolism, aids sluggish digestion, and supports natural lactation.
uses: Maintains healthy blood sugar levels, reduces cholesterol, and supports nursing mothers.
preparation: Soak 1 teaspoon seeds in water overnight and drink water with seeds in the morning.
safety_notes: May aggravate Pitta due to heat; monitor glucose levels if taking insulin.

name: Coriander (Dhania)
description: Cooling herb that soothes acidity, reduces digestive heat, and relieves urinary discomfort.
uses: Cools hyperacidity, relieves burning urination, eases heat stress, and aids digestion.
preparation: Soak crushed seeds in water overnight to make cold infusion (Hima).
safety_notes: Safe for long-term use; very gentle on the digestive system.

name: Cumin (Jeera)
description: Stimulates secretion of digestive enzymes, reduces abdominal bloating, and aids nutrient absorption.
uses: Relieves flatulence, treats abdominal cramps, aids post-meal digestion, and boosts Agni.
preparation: Boil 1 teaspoon cumin seeds in 1 liter water for daily drinking (Jeera Water).
safety_notes: Excessive raw seed consumption can lead to minor heartburn in sensitive Pitta types.

name: Curry Leaves (Kadi Patta)
description: Supports liver health, strengthens hair roots, and maintains balanced blood glucose levels.
uses: Prevents hair thinning, supports digestive enzyme release, and protects liver tissue.
preparation: Chew 5-6 fresh washed leaves raw daily or incorporate into daily cooking.
safety_notes: Extremely safe for daily culinary use.

name: Black Pepper (Maricha)
description: Clears respiratory congestion, increases bio-availability of herbs, and kindles sluggish digestion.
uses: Clears sinus pressure, breaks down thick mucus, and improves bioavailability of curcumin.
preparation: Add a pinch of fresh ground black pepper to warm teas, honey, or meals.
safety_notes: Aggravates Pitta heat; avoid in stomach ulcers and gastritis.

name: Cinnamon (Twak)
description: Improves peripheral circulation, stabilizes glucose spikes, and warms cold digestion.
uses: Warms cold extremities, improves blood circulation, and aids glycemic control.
preparation: Simmer a small stick in water for 10 minutes to prepare a warm aromatic tea.
safety_notes: Use Ceylon Cinnamon to avoid high coumarin levels found in Cassia varieties.

name: Clove (Lavanga)
description: Natural oral analgesic, reduces toothaches, and clears throat irritation and coughs.
uses: Soothes toothaches, relieves throat tickle, suppresses cough, and freshens oral cavity.
preparation: Hold 1 whole clove in the cheek for oral relief or use diluted clove oil locally.
safety_notes: Undiluted oil is potent and can irritate delicate mucous membranes.

name: Licorice (Mulethi / Yashtimadhu)
description: Soothes sore throat hoarseness, protects gastric mucus lining, and relieves acid reflux.
uses: Eases dry cough, coat inflamed vocal cords, relieves heart burn, and soothes ulcers.
preparation: Chew on a small root piece or steep 1/2 teaspoon powder in warm water.
safety_notes: Prolonged high doses may cause fluid retention and elevated blood pressure.

name: Bael (Bilva)
description: Highly effective for intestinal health, soothing irritable bowel conditions, and managing diarrhea.
uses: Relieves chronic diarrhea, dysentery, IBS symptoms, and tones the intestine wall.
preparation: Consume unripe fruit pulp sherbet or leaf decoction as prescribed.
safety_notes: Excess ripe fruit pulp can cause severe constipation.

name: Shankhpushpi
description: Supports deep restful sleep, calms hyperactive thinking, and reduces stress-induced memory lapses.
uses: Eases mental hypertension, improves sleep latency, calms panic, and sharpens intellect.
preparation: Mix 1/2 teaspoon powder with warm milk or water before sleep.
safety_notes: May cause mild sedation; use caution when driving or operating machinery.

name: Gotu Kola (Mandukaparni)
description: Promotes skin elasticity, collagen synthesis, wound recovery, and cognitive function.
uses: Supports micro-circulation, heals skin lesions, reduces varicose veins, and boosts focus.
preparation: Brew fresh or dried leaves into an infusion or consume fresh leaf paste.
safety_notes: Avoid high doses in individuals with active liver conditions.

name: Manjistha
description: Primary lymphatic cleanser and blood purifier that helps clarify skin complexion.
uses: Purifies stagnant lymph, clears stubborn skin eruptions, and supports female cycle balance.
preparation: Take 1/2 teaspoon root powder with warm water after meals.
safety_notes: May turn urine reddish/brown harmlessly due to natural plant pigments.

name: Vasaka (Adhatoda Vasica)
description: Powerful bronchodilator for relieving chronic asthma symptoms, bronchitis, and excess phlegm.
uses: Opens airways, eases asthmatic wheezing, thins stubborn phlegm, and stops cough.
preparation: Express 5-10 ml fresh leaf juice and combine with 1 teaspoon honey.
safety_notes: Has oxytocic properties; strictly avoid during pregnancy.

name: Sarpagandha (Rauvolfia serpentina)
description: Classical potent herb used under guidance for calming severe nervous excitement and high pressure.
uses: Reduces high blood pressure, manages severe insomnia, and calms acute agitation.
preparation: Administered strictly in micro-doses under supervision of a Vaidya.
safety_notes: STRICT WARNING: Potent alkaloid content. Do not self-administer; requires professional prescription.
